segments.title: Chương 70: Thăm Họ Hàng
segments.content:
The cluster of dwellings where Chen Guiliang's family lived was called Manzi Tuo, located between the three administrative groups of their village.

The terrain was secluded and narrow, home to a total of only seven households.

These seven households had all branched out from brothers splitting up their families and belonged to three different village groups.

There were, however, quite a few tombs nearby.

Especially the ancient ethnic minority tombs, commonly known as "Manzi Caves."

There were also some Han Chinese tombs, but most had already been plundered.

When Chen Guiliang was in elementary school, he even crawled into a looted ancient tomb, took out a skull, and brought it to school, scaring many students into wailing and crying. He was then severely reprimanded by the teacher and his palms were struck twenty times.

When he returned the skull to the tomb, he pulled out a tooth as a souvenir. His parents found out, and he got another sound beating.

From this, it was evident that Hero Chen had been a reckless punk since he was a child; that crazy personality seemed to be innate.

During the New Year holiday, apart from visiting his maternal grandparents to pay his respects, Chen Guiliang stayed cooped up at home writing a game design document.

Occasionally, elementary school classmates would drop by for a visit.

This was because when Chen Guiliang was in elementary school, he had always been the king of the kids at school.

His battle for prestige was the time he brought a skull to school—anyone who dared to challenge him got a dead man's head shoved in their face!

"Ge, let's go."

"Coming, coming."

On the sixth day of the Lunar New Year, they had arranged to visit their paternal grandmother's maiden home, which included Second Uncle and Aunt's families as well.

Since Grandma got carsick, everyone had to walk, a trek that took a full four hours.

It was a village next to the district city, relatively affluent compared to the more remote rural areas.

"Zuzu, Yigong, Yipo, Biaoshu..."

"Come quickly to burn paper money for the ancestors and have the meal!"

Grandma's mother was customarily called Zuzu here.

Zuzu was over eighty this year, born a landlord's daughter, and had even had her feet bound in her youth.

She naturally married a landlord's son, but her husband was a rather wild character. During the War of Resistance, when Sichuan salt was in short supply, he actually gathered a group of men to smuggle it.

One could only say they were exceptionally wealthy.

When Feng Yuxiang came to Longdu to call for donations for the war effort, not only did Zuzu's family donate several hundred silver dollars, but she herself also donated a gold ring and a pair of gold bracelets.

Later, during the Liberation, they donated another two hundred silver dollars to the People's Government.

They didn't suffer any particular calamities. The family didn't own much land, and they were even allowed to keep a portion of it during the land reform.

But they had a lot of silver currency. Until the 1980s, Zuzu still had over a hundred silver dollars hidden away, but they were stolen in the early 1990s. All that was left were a few silver dollars hidden by each of her four daughters to "dispel wind."

In comparison, Grandpa's side was the real major landlord family.

But their luck was quite good. Both of Grandpa's parents were opium addicts and had squandered the entire family fortune. When class components were assigned, they were directly classified as poor peasants...

Although Grandpa had never been to school, his several older brothers and sisters had all received good educations and became teachers and workers in the city after the founding of the PRC.

Due to his status as a stepson, Father rarely visited Grandpa's relatives in the city.

"Liangliang, I heard you won first prize. Are Tsinghua and Peking University fighting to get you?" Third Yigong asked.

Third Yigong was Feng Tao's father, a leading figure in the village.

He knew a little about fortune-telling and traditional Chinese medicine, had excellent calligraphy, and was always called upon to mediate neighborhood disputes.

Chen Guiliang replied, "There's no definite news from Tsinghua or Peking University yet, but Fudan and Beijing Normal University do intend to admit me."

Third Yigong said, "Fudan is quite good. After graduation, you'll be assigned a job in a big city."

His thinking was still stuck in the era of guaranteed job assignments. He then turned to praise Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan, "You two have educated him very well. Your son has great prospects."

Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan just smiled. When Third Yigong spoke, everyone else had to listen obediently.

Grandma had no brothers, but she had three younger sisters.

Second Yigong and Fourth Yigong were both honest, down-to-earth farmers.

Third Yigong then said to the other children, "You kids, you must learn from your older brother. Chen Guirong, of all of you still in school, besides your older brother, you're the oldest. How are your grades?"

His cousin Chen Guirong buried his head in his food, "They're okay."

"Okay means not okay. If you don't study hard, you'll just end up back in the countryside tilling the earth!" Third Yigong lectured.

Chen Guirong's scalp tingled. He had been intimidated by this Yigong since he was a child.

"Nie Wei, what about you?" Third Yigong then asked Second Yigong's grandson.

He asked them one by one, and none of the children dared to speak.

Third Yigong continued to praise Chen Guiliang, making Chen Xinghua and Yao Lan feel a sense of pride. At this moment, the hardships of the past few years all seemed to count for nothing.

Feng Tao shot Chen Guiliang a knowing look.

After lunch, Third Yigong called Chen Guiliang into his bedroom (which also served as a study) and said enthusiastically, "Come here, I've written a piece of calligraphy for you."

Chen Guiliang took it and saw that the content was very cliché: The mountain of books has a path, and diligence is the way; the sea of learning is boundless, and hard work is the boat.

As for the calligraphy, it was certainly better than Chen Guiliang's own terrible handwriting.

Third Yigong then pulled Chen Guiliang aside to brag, telling him some strange and bizarre stories, and then quizzed Chen Guiliang on Zi Wei Dou Shu—this was also something he had taught him, which Chen Guiliang had learned cursorily in junior high.

Aside from bluffing people, it was utterly useless.

Alright, it actually had a little bit of use. It taught Chen Guiliang how to calculate the Heavenly Stems and Earthly Branches.

Hadn't he used it when writing the preface for his poem in the New Concept Composition Contest?

Feng Tao, however, never learned it and considered his father a charlatan. If he was really so amazing, why didn't any villagers ask him for feng shui consultations or to read their horoscopes? No one sought him out for medical treatment either; villagers would rather see a barefoot doctor when they were sick.

Chen Guiliang found an opportunity to make a bathroom escape.

He had no common topics with Third Yigong. He still remembered arguing with him about international issues back in his first year of high school; the old and the young had almost started a full-blown quarrel on the spot.

This was an elderly armchair politician and a peacemaker for the surrounding villages. But his main occupation was a farmer, and he still had to work in the fields.

In the courtyard, Zuzu, Grandma, the Yipos, Mother, Aunt, the Biao-yis, and the Shen-shens were chatting, while the men had set up tables and started playing mahjong.

Chen Guiliang went over to chat with them.

Mainly to keep Zuzu company.

Among all his relatives and elders, Zuzu was the one who treated him best, and also the one who treated his father best. When his father got beaten at home as a child, he would walk for hours to Zuzu's place to complain and lick his wounds.

Zuzu wouldn't live for many more years. She would pass away peacefully at the age of 90, which in the countryside was considered a joyous funeral.

"Liangliang, if you go to study at Fudan, you'll become a 'Magic City' person in the future," a Biao-yi said jokingly.

Biaoshen Lin Chunhong said, "You all don't know yet, Liangliang made a game with Boss Tao and earned over a hundred thousand in two months!"

"Really?"

The elders were instantly amazed, followed by another round of praise.

The relatives on this side were quite harmonious, and no one asked Chen Guiliang for money.

Actually, the relatives on Grandpa's side were also quite harmonious, it was just that they treated Chen Guiliang and his father as outsiders. Among themselves, they had always helped each other out, even arranging for several younger family members to get jobs in state-owned enterprises.

Zuzu sat in the courtyard basking in the sun, watching the bustling conversation among the younger generations. She opened her mouth, revealing her toothless gums, and smiled continuously.

"Bang!"

A rascal kid suddenly threw a firecracker, startling the elders.

It was Fourth Yigong's grandson, who was quickly caught and given a sound beating.

The other children, including Chen Guirong, burst out laughing. They were the ones who had instigated it!

In a flash, it was the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, and school was about to start.

During this time, some former creditors came to their door. Most came to mend their relationship with Chen Xinghua, but a very few came to ask for interest—Chen Guiliang had said he would pay it.

"Dad, Mom, you don't need to go work as migrant laborers anymore," Chen Guiliang said.

Yao Lan smiled, "We won't go. We'll just farm here at home."

She knew her son had money and no longer had to worry about tuition and living expenses for university.

Chen Xinghua looked at their dilapidated house, "I still have to go work for a few more years. I can't use your money to build a house."

He had his pride. After working as a laborer for so many years, his son had helped pay off the debts, and now he was supposed to let his son pay for building a house. What would be the value of his own life then?

Chen Guiliang understood his father's thoughts. "How about this, you two stay at home and rent one of the brigade's factory buildings to raise rabbits. You don't need to do it on a large scale. I'll invest ten or twenty thousand yuan, and it won't matter even if we lose money. If you make money, then you can use that to build a new house."

Here in Longdu, every household would raise rabbits. It was only after going out to work as migrant laborers became popular that household farming decreased.

And there was no worry about sales. Everyone here ate rabbit; not a single rabbit could get out of here alive!

As for the village's factory buildings, that was a sore spot in the hearts of all the villagers.

In the 1980s, rural enterprises were blooming everywhere. A boss from Fujian province persuaded a certain cadre from the commune. That cadre brought the Fujian boss back to the village and enthusiastically raised funds to open a glass factory.

Many villagers were duped, some even taking out loans to invest.

Then, the Fujian boss ran off with the money, leaving behind only a few empty factory buildings, a bunch of villagers who had lost their shirts, and some who were saddled with loans of several hundred or even a thousand yuan.

That commune cadre, in his anger, hanged himself!

Chen Xinghua looked at his wife.

Yao Lan really didn't want to go out to work as a laborer again. She said, "Let's give it a try. I might not be good at other things, but I'm quite skilled at raising rabbits. I've been cutting grass to raise rabbits since I was little. First for the production team, then for myself. It's much easier than raising pigs."

Chen Guiliang said, "Large-scale breeding is different. Dad will need to go to other rabbit farms to investigate first. Don't raise too many in the first year, two or three hundred will be enough. You can expand production once you have more experience."

Chen Xinghua smoked his cigarette and thought for a long time.

He had extremely strong self-esteem and wanted to achieve something in his life, otherwise, he wouldn't have partnered with someone to subcontract small projects in the mid-90s.

If he had to rely on his son for everything, Chen Xinghua would feel uneasy.

But thinking of his wife who had toiled alongside him for so many years, and his elderly mother who had been managing the household, Chen Xinghua could only agree, "Then let's raise rabbits!"

On the sixteenth day of the first lunar month, Chen Guiliang bid farewell to his parents and grandmother and once again took the dilapidated bus back to school.

Over at Xihua City Daily, reporter Chen Feng's article was also about to be published.

(I am fortunate to be lumped together with Er Gen and Lao Gui in fabricated rumors, which shows that Lao Wang has achieved some small success. I'm secretly pleased. But we don't have a custom of engagement here, nor have I ever seen anyone get engaged, so please stop spreading rumors that I got engaged and was cheated on.)

(This chapter is a transitional one, introducing the living environment and family background...)
